We realize this methodology through Semantic Context Annotations (SemTexts), a dedicated language mechanism independent of documentation and schema metadata. SemTexts associate natural-language instructions with individual program entities and use declaration scopes to determine where they apply. Our implementation extends the Jac compiler and MTP runtime to preserve these associations and select applicable guidance during automatic prompt construction. We evaluate Semantic Engineering on seven AI-integrated applications and two standard benchmarks across three models. Across the applications, it achieves a 5.46-fold reduction in integration lines of code relative to Prompt Engineering while delivering equal or better task performance in most model-application settings, reaching up to 1.83 times the task performance of Prompt Engineering.

Software Engineering.title: Claude for Excel is Transformative for Basic Spreadsheet Modeling and Analysis
Software Engineering.summary: We used the Claude Excel plug-in to build and analyze spreadsheet models for five semi structured problem statements (including a test-piece teaching case with data in multiple exhibits) and evaluated performance on modeling (what is to be coded), spreadsheet engineering (quality of coding), analysis (algorithms applied to the spreadsheet), and insight generation. Claude's ability to create a high-quality spreadsheet model from a semi structured problem statement is astoundingly excellent. Given very simple prompts, Claude generates extensive, accurate sensitivity and scenario analyses and reasonable plain English insights. Claude is Solver-aware and builds optimization models without specific prompting. Analyst productivity gains will likely be high. Business school quant courses will have to change. The way we develop human expertise will have to change.

Software Engineering.title: A Compact Formula-Aware Spreadsheet Abstraction for Large Language Models
Software Engineering.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to assist spreadsheet users with tasks such as spreadsheet model construction, formula generation, and data analysis, yet their interaction with real-world spreadsheets remains limited by the mismatch between the structure of spreadsheets and the sequential textual representations typically provided to LLMs. We propose a compact formula-aware spreadsheet abstraction that represents large homogeneous ranges through their positions, types, R1C1 formula patterns, and selected boundary values. An efficient algorithm detects and structures these ranges before a textual serialization is supplied to an LLM. The abstraction is provided to the LLM before detailed spreadsheet content is submitted, improving the accuracy and efficiency of spreadsheet processing while reducing token consumption. We evaluate the method on 50 spreadsheet-query cases. The evaluation shows that the abstraction alone was sufficient to answer some queries. When additional spreadsheet content is required, the abstraction reduces the amount of data that must be submitted to the LLM, thereby reducing token consumption. The abstraction layer also improves the reliability and accuracy of spreadsheet processing. We conclude by discussing further techniques for combining spreadsheet static analysis with artificial intelligence to improve the reliability, accuracy, and efficiency of AI assisted spreadsheet tasks.

Operating Systems.title: High-Throughput Private Information Retrieval with on-CPU Accelerators
Operating Systems.summary: Private information retrieval (PIR) hides which record a client retrieves by scanning the entire database, and batching is an effective technique to improve throughput by sharing this scan across queries. However, existing CPU-based solutions gain little from batching because each query still requires its own multiplications, and vector instructions perform only a few at a time. GPUs and other discrete accelerators can accelerate these computations, but require extra hardware and can constrain database size due to their limited memory capacity. In this paper, we present AltoPIR, the first PIR system that leverages on-CPU matrix accelerators such as Intel AMX. AltoPIR keeps the accelerator fed from the CPU caches, reading each database byte from memory once for all queries in a batch and never writing intermediate products to memory. This enables high-performance PIR through efficient batching without requiring discrete accelerators. Our evaluation shows that AltoPIR achieves up to 50.1x higher throughput than existing CPU-based solutions and serves databases larger than a GPU's memory.

Performance.title: Sonar-MoE: In-Backward Expert Updates for Memory-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Training
Performance.summary: Most parameters of a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model belong to its experts, and standard training keeps every expert gradient in GPU memory until the optimizer step. This memory grows with the number and size of the experts, so it rises as MoE models scale. We introduce Sonar-MoE, which updates each expert tensor during the backward pass and frees its gradient right away. It brings optimizer-in-backward from dense models to batched MoE expert tensors, so the GPU never holds more than one layer of expert gradients. When we fine-tune OLMoE-1B-7B and Granite-3.1-3B-A800M in bf16 with two expert-kernel backends, Sonar-MoE lowers peak memory by 19% to 22%. Its updates are bitwise identical to standard training without expert gradient clipping, and held-out loss stays within 0.003 of all baselines. Each step also takes 17% to 23% less time than standard training with global-norm clipping. Updating whole batched tensors rather than individual experts is what keeps Sonar-MoE fast, as it avoids a 20% to 72% slowdown while using the same memory. Sonar-MoE matches optimizer-in-backward over all parameters in memory and speed while still clipping the dense parameters.

Performance.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Signing and Verification Performance of Verifiable Credential Formats: A Cross-Language Benchmark of SD-JWT VC, W3C VCDM, and mdoc
Performance.summary: We compare the signing and verification performance of three Verifiable Credential (VC) formats--SD-JWT VC; the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 with a Data Integrity cryptosuite (W3C VCDM); and mdoc (ISO/IEC 18013-5)--over one scope: issue, present with selective disclosure, verify. Node.js, Go and Python implementations ran in four environments, one a cloud VM (N=2,000 across five runs; medians of each statistic and the spread). For an end-to-end exchange disclosing 5 of 20 attributes, the total (issue, present, verify) on Node.js in the cloud VM is 0.265 ms for mdoc, 0.298 ms for SD-JWT VC and 0.534 ms for W3C VCDM. The four span a factor of five in speed; across them W3C VCDM takes 1.73--2.04x mdoc and 1.57--1.79x SD-JWT VC--at least five times our 10% band--and the ordering survives unifying the algorithm on Ed25519 and P-256. The mdoc--SD-JWT VC difference is not robust: the totals differ by 12%, 28%, 19% and 10% in the four environments, and at verification mdoc is the slower in one of them. RDFC-1.0 canonicalization produces the gap: the cryptosuite canonicalizes twice per operation, so one exchange canonicalizes six times. We attribute that cost to the specification rather than to a library mainly by replacing RDFC-1.0 with JCS, which brings W3C VCDM verification to within 5% of SD-JWT VC in three environments and within 12% in the fourth; three implementations in three languages agree, though they share a lineage. Because eddsa-rdfc-2022 has no derivation step, presenting a subset re-signs it; ecdsa-sd-2023, which preserves the issuer signature, costs 3.4 ms to issue and 1.5--2.4 ms to derive and verify there. With production education schemas, canonicalization costs 31--49x a simple credential across the four, and blank node labeling is not the driver. The measured path ends at the issuer signature check.
Performance.comment: 31 pages, 4 figures, 19 tables. Measurement kit and raw result files: https://github.com/fujie/vcbench

Performance.title: CrowdForge: Effects of Audio and Visual Audience Participation Modalities on Agency, Collaboration, and Engagement in AI-Mediated MR Performances
Performance.summary: Technology-mediated audience participation (TMAP) enables audiences to influence live performances, yet balancing interaction with meaningful agency remains challenging. While AI-generated music and MR enable new forms of audio and visual audience participation, little is known about how these participation modalities influence audience experiences during live musical performance. In particular, it remains unclear how they shape perceived agency, collaboration, and engagement, and how they complement one another within TMAP systems. We present CrowdForge, an AI- and MR-mediated paradigm where audiences collectively control generative music and virtual environments during a live performance featuring a guitarist and DJ. Through a mixedmethods concert study evaluating three interaction conditions (audio, visual, and combined audio-visual), we demonstrate that observability is the primary driver of audience agency. While visual interaction provided easily observable feedback, audio parameters offered macro-structural control over the music. Audiences tended to use the control enabled by AI audio generation to test musical boundaries, introducing a productive adversarial tension between the crowd and the musicians. This dynamic pushed creative limits, deepened engagement, and generated moments of musical coherence when performers successfully resolved audience-induced challenges. We argue future TMAP systems should prioritize human-centered, highly observable interactions to build agency, while combining the expressiveness of music with the clarity of visual feedback.

Performance.title: The SIMPLE Law for Energy Cost of LLM Inference
Performance.summary: Generative AI is billed per token, yet tokens are not equally expensive. Each token enters the KV-cache and raises the cost of those that follow, so energy grows non-linearly along a sequence whose tokens look identical. No analytical model states what a token costs, and the most accurate SOTA model is a fit, not a law: it absorbs architecture into fitted coefficients, requiring per-LLM fitting. We derive closed-form expressions of the computational and memory-access complexity of LLM inference in terms of architectural hyperparameters, covering MHA and GQA, and compare a family of analytical models of increasing granularity. From these, we obtain the SIMPLE Inference Model to Predict LLMs Energy (SIMPLE), a four-parameter law that separates prefill from decode, and decode into KV-cache cost and next-token computation. Over traces of 13 dense LLMs from six families on NVIDIA H100 GPUs, it attains R2 = 0.969 and 11.97% MAPE, 3.1-3.5x below the SOTA, without per-LLM calibration. The SIMPLE law explains as well as predicts: prefill energy grows quadratically with the hidden dimension, so larger LLMs suffer most from long inputs; and more aggressive GQA KV grouping reduces the per-token energy by up to 3x relative to standard MHA. Increasing the reasoning token budget pushes output length beyond the analytically derived energy minimum, driving super-linear energy growth; although accuracy grows with the budget, energy grows faster, so Intelligence per Joule peaks at an intermediate budget and falls by up to 3.14x across a 4.0x reasoning-budget range. Agentic serving raises energy per request by 13.0x relative to non-agentic ones, driven by the growth of both the prefill and the KV-cache terms with input length; while prefix caching removes most of the prefill cost (-93%), the KV-cache term is unaffected, so even a cached agentic request costs 4.8x more.
Performance.comment: Submitted to Future Generation Computer Systems

Performance.title: Local Zero-Shot Latency Prediction for Low-End GPUs
Performance.summary: Quantifying execution latency is an important consideration across Machine Learning. Existing latency-prediction approaches typically train ML models on traces collected from workload execution on target hardware. Collection of representative traces across many consumer GPUs is expensive both in organizing the devices and in manpower, causing existing work to mainly focus on a limited set of high-end GPUs available in cloud computing. To offset this cost, we show that a local host GPU can be configured to reproduce the execution performance of less powerful target GPUs. Through selectively modifying device parameters, we obtain locally measured latencies that closely approximate those observed on the target hardware. We reformulate the latency-prediction task: instead of fitting a prediction model to a dataset of execution traces, we identify local configurations that best reproduce target devices' performance, enabling zero-shot prediction. We evaluate our approach against real measurements from 60 computer-vision models executed on 21 consumer GPU models. Our method achieves a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 14.21%, compared with more than 25% for comparable baselines, reducing relative prediction error by 43.6%. Predicted and measured latencies exhibit an average Spearman correlation of 0.961 across training tasks, demonstrating that the method also accurately preserves performance rankings across devices.

Performance.title: HPC-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for High Performance Computing Codes
Performance.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong capabilities in code generation and reasoning, motivating extensive benchmarks for evaluating functional correctness. However, performance optimization in High-Performance Computing (HPC) poses fundamentally different challenges that are not captured by existing evaluations: HPC performance depends on low-level code, intricate memory access patterns, and computational kernels embedded within sophisticated execution contexts. We introduce HPC-Bench, a performance-grounded benchmark for evaluating LLMs as optimizers of computational kernels in realistic HPC workloads, including 114 workloads across 16 HPC computational motifs. HPC-Bench provides a fully automated, end-to-end evaluation pipeline that combines program-level correctness verification with two correctness-gated metrics, Fast@k and Speedup@k, to characterize reliability and speedup under a fixed sampling budget. Our evaluation of three representative LLMs across serial CPU, OpenMP, and CUDA settings shows that stricter speedup requirements substantially reduce the probability of finding a correct and fast optimization. HPC-Bench is available at https://github.com/Deep-Learning-Profiling-Tools/HPC-Bench.
Performance.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations & Datasets Track (poster). 31 pages, 13 figures, 19 tables

Performance.title: Understanding the Energy Cost of Quantized Agents on Shared GPUs
Performance.summary: Quantization can lower the energy of language-model calls and free memory for serving more agents, but its benefit per completed task remains unclear when agents share a GPU. Measurements of fixed requests or isolated agents leave open how the agents' generated work interact with competition for compute and cache. We present a systematic study of precision and admission limits for two agent models on A100 deployments with 40 or 80 GB of memory, using coding and data-analysis tasks with independently verified outcomes. We replay recorded calls across precisions to isolate execution energy and cap the cache to test the value of freed memory. For both models with four admitted agents where requests fit in the cache, 4-bit weights with 16-bit activations execute the same calls with 10-25% less energy than 8-bit weights and activations. Despite this saving, extra work and fewer completions in live runs raise their energy per verified completion by 49%. Where requests compete for cache on the 40 GB deployment, 4-bit weights cost less, and capping their cache raises energy per verified completion by 34% with 16 agents. These results show how generated work and cache demand change the energy benefit of quantization, providing a practical basis for choosing precision and admission limits together.
Performance.comment: 16 pages, 8 figures. Alex Flesher and Aldric Yang contributed equally

Performance.title: Exploring the Power Consumption of ERC-4337 Bundling on Server Infrastructure
Performance.summary: The Ethereum ecosystem offers the most widespread support for Decentralised Applications (DApps), with over 120 networks currently documented as using variants of the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) for core execution logic. The ERC-4337 standard provides convenient access to DApps for users who do not possess the required cryptocurrency or prefer flexible authorisation of DApp actions. The infrastructure for ERC-4337 implementation can be deployed on any EVM network. However, to aggregate user requests and submit them to the EVM network, ERC-4337 requires operating a bundler, an additional component. Recently, the potential use of ERC-4337 was boosted by another standard, EIP-7702, which can enable ERC-4337 utility for any existing user account. However, the use of the combined EIP-7702/ERC-4337 pattern remains considerably low at less than 6% of EIP-7702 activity. We believe that this underutilisation is at least partly caused by the low number of existing bundling services and their popularity, currently fewer than 15 publicly documented. Expanding the number of bundler nodes would benefit the ecosystem but would introduce operational costs, part of which is represented by the added nodes' power consumption. In this paper, we provide a thorough view of the bundling power consumption aspect using server-grade infrastructure, evaluating both CPU and RAM consumption, as well as the overhead of container-based deployments specific to production environments.
Performance.comment: Accepted for the 8th International Conference on Blockchain Computing and Applications, BCCA 2026; Copyright is with IEEE

Performance.title: MaxKernel: Agentic Kernel Generation for TPUs
Performance.summary: Designing and authoring high-performance custom kernels for accelerators is a complex task that requires deep hardware-level expertise. Large Language Models (LLM) can be leveraged together with real-time compiler feedback to build agentic systems for kernel generation. In this work, we present MaxKernel, a multi-agent system that implements three distinct paradigms for TPU kernel development: (1) a Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) agent for collaborative, step-by-step design; (2) an Autonomous (Auto) agent that executes a fully automated, metric/trace-driven optimization loop; and (3) a Graph-Based Autonomous Search that scales the Auto agent for global exploration of the design space. All three paradigms leverage a shared pool of specialized sub-agents to handle planning, implementation, self-debugging, testing, and hardware profiling. We evaluate MaxKernel on JaxBench, a comprehensive suite of 50 diverse kernel tasks for TPUs, alongside complex, real-world workloads from state-of-the-art open-source models. We demonstrate that MaxKernel consistently generates highly optimized implementations, matching expert hand-tuned baselines and delivering significant performance across the benchmark. Our agent is open-sourced and available https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/accelerator-agents/tree/main/MaxKernel.
Performance.comment: 14 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables

Performance.title: Unlocking Turing Tensor Cores: A Measured Throughput Account of From-Scratch Pre-training on a Single 22G RTX 2080 Ti
Performance.summary: The RTX 2080 Ti (TU102) ships full second-generation Tensor Cores in hardware, yet the vendor throttles FP16 matrix multiplication at the driver level, leaving usable tensor throughput well below the hardware peak. turing-unlock lifts this restriction with a kernel module that, before the nvidia driver binds the device, writes the FP16 speed selectors (SS0=0x88888888, SS1=0x8) and releases the ACR mutex; published measurements report cuBLAS FP16 matmul throughput rising from 55.7 to 91.4 TFLOPS (about 1.6x). On the same 22G 2080 Ti and under the same from-scratch pre-training protocol as the companion memory ledger (five tiers of Chinese encoder-decoder models, 2,451 steps per tier, 16,384 tokens per step, seed 42), we obtain a before/after throughput account: the small tier (75.7M parameters, 512-wide, 8+8 layers, activation checkpointing on) improves in steady-state throughput from 6,480 to 7,246 tok/s (+11.8%) with wall time cut from 1.77h to 1.61h (9.0% saved); the tiny tier goes from 15,150 to 15,866 tok/s (+4.7%) with wall time savings of 3.8%; the three smaller tiers (pico-micro) gain at most +0.3%; per-tier peak memory stays bit-identical, and final quality metrics are bit-identical or consistent within 10^-3. We conclude that the unlock gain is a function of matrix size, rising monotonically with tier -- imperceptible for pico-micro, visible from tiny upward, and cashed out as a double-digit percentage at small -- and that it is a pure throughput gain that leaves training dynamics untouched.
Performance.comment: 7 pages, 4 tables

Hardware Architecture.title: Beyond MACs: Deployment-Constrained Design Space Exploration for Tensorized Neural Networks
Hardware Architecture.summary: Tensor-train (TT) compression reduces neural-network parameters, but the latency of a tensorized layer is set by its contraction order and its mapping onto hardware: a contraction path with fewer multiply-accumulate operations (MACs) is not necessarily faster on a systolic array. We present a deployment-constrained, latency-guided design space exploration (DSE) framework for fixed-rank tensorized neural networks (TNNs) under a fixed processing-element (PE) budget. Using MAC-guided path pruning, it evaluates feasible combinations of contraction paths, three PE-array partitions, and input-, output-, and weight-stationary dataflows. By minimizing the sum of inference and training latency estimates, it selects a single physical PE partition shared across layers and both modes, while allowing layer- and mode-specific paths and dataflows. On ResNet-18 and ViT-Ti/4, 25%-50% of the layers select a path other than the minimum-MAC one, the best dataflow varies across layers and models, and on a representative ViT layer the latency-selected candidate reduces simulated latency by 23.5% relative to the minimum-MAC candidate. Deployed on a Xilinx VU9P FPGA accelerator that supports both inference and training, the complete TT+INT8 system achieves 3.28x-4.00x inference and 3.42x-3.85x training speedups over dense implementations with the same PE budget.

Hardware Architecture.title: A Cross-Domain Matrix Engine for Signal Processing and Deep Neural Net Inference
Hardware Architecture.summary: Matrix multiplication dominates both PHY signal processing and Deep Neural Network (DNN) inference, yet these domains place opposing demands on the matrix engine. Signal processing requires low-latency execution of relatively small matrix operations, whereas DNN inference, particularly at large batch sizes, prioritizes high throughput and energy efficiency for large matrix multiplications. While offering efficient memory access profile, a Systolic Array (SA) adds fill and drain delays per matrix. Those can be amortized for large matrices but not for small matrices. Conversely, a tensor unit completes the kernel in few cycles but would require repeated reads of same operand tiles over large matrices. This makes SA too slow for signal processing and tensor too inefficient for AI. We show that this need not be a choice between systolic and tensor structuring of Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) units. We propose a single engine that operates primarily as a SA and, through low-cost reconfiguration, transforms into a tensor-style engine on a per-operation basis. MUXes create both the spatial reduction adder tree and temporal reduction accumulators from the existing MACs and registers within the systolic array. The proposed reconfigurable SA simulated using modified SCALESim simulator, verified on an Zynq 702 FPGA and synthesized using ASAP 7nm FinFET library. SCALE-Sim simulations shows up to 7.5x lower latency for small complex value PHY kernels. Even on DNN workloads, it achieves up to 1.65x speedups over vanilla SA execution with trivial increase of memory accesses, retaining the systolic array's memory access advantage. Synthesis results estimate reconfigurable fabric costs only 8% power and 13.6% area overheads.

Hardware Architecture.title: In-depth data movement characterization of DNA read mapping algorithms
Hardware Architecture.summary: Read mapping algorithms represent a critical bottleneck in genomic analysis pipelines due to the resources required; a problem that is becoming more pronounced as sequencing technologies advance and datasets expand. We present an extensive workload characterization of leading read mapping algorithms across diverse sequencing technologies to identify hardware acceleration and optimization opportunities. We analyzed the following implementations: MashMap, wfmash, and Minimap2 for whole-genome alignment (WGA); NGMLR, Minimap2, and LRA for long reads; and Bowtie2, BWA-MEM, StrobeAlign, and minibwa for short reads. We used the Intel VTune Profiler for detailed memory analysis to identify memory- bound functions, cache usage patterns, and data transfer bottlenecks. We further analyzed a selected subset of alignment tools using the DAMOV-SIM simulator to obtain a more granular view of data movement characteristics for two different cache structures. Based on our results, Minimap2 emerges as the fastest alignment tool for long read scenarios, but falls behind in whole-genome alignment due to poor multithreading. Across all three categories, some programs (e.g., LRA, BWA-MEM) are highly memory-bound. More in-depth analysis via DAMOV-SIM revealed that some memory-bound tools, in particular, do not fully utilize the multi-level cache hierarchy in modern multi-core CPU architectures. Our results show that while some tools require algorithmic redesign for performance gains, some others can benefit from running on PIM architectures.

Hardware Architecture.title: TinyML Hits the Memory Wall: A Benchmark of Ten Sub-Watt Edge Devices
Hardware Architecture.summary: Neural network inference at the edge must fit tight energy budgets. Existing benchmarks compare few devices, do not report energy on a common basis, and omit the newest microcontrollers with an NPU or the 1 GHz Cortex-M85. Hardware-aware design also ranks networks by MAC count, yet no study has tested whether this proxy holds across accelerators. We benchmark sub-watt edge AI hardware by evaluating four CNNs (MobileNetV3, MCUNetV1, EfficientNet, SqueezeNet) and two tiny transformers (MobileViT-XXS, DeiT-tiny) on ten commercial devices: an in-sensor DSP (Sony IMX500), four MCUs with an NPU (STM32N6, Alif Ensemble E7/E8, GreenWaves GAP9), and five MCUs without an NPU (STM32U5, Apollo510B, ESP32-S3 Xtensa LX7, RA8M2, STM32V8). Four devices are novel (Alif E8, Apollo510B, RA8M2, STM32V8). Measured as energy above idle, the IMX500 (0.13-0.35 mJ) uses 1.3-3x less energy than the STM32N6 (0.31-1.05 mJ) on every model; the GAP9 uses the least on MobileNetV3 and the Alif E7 the least on MCUNetV1 and SqueezeNet. All four use 6-34x less energy than the STM32V8 (1.85-3.98 mJ), and the Alif E7 and IMX500 form the power-performance Pareto front. Latency on all four accelerators scales with memory traffic (bytes of weights and activations, r >= 0.98) and not with MACs, so they are memory-bound, while no MCU without an NPU is. The NPU advantage grows with intensity from 1.4x over a 1 GHz Cortex-M85 on MCUNetV1 to 8.2x on SqueezeNet. MAC count is therefore a misleading cost proxy for sub-watt accelerators.

Hardware Architecture.title: End-to-End NTT on FPGA for FHE Acceleration
Hardware Architecture.summary: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables privacy-preserving computation on encrypted data without decryption. Despite its strong security guarantees, FHE incurs substantial computational and memory overhead. In FHE-based deep learning inference, on average 63% of the CPU time is spent on the number theoretic transform (NTT) and its inverse (INTT), which reduce the complexity of polynomial multiplication from $O(N^2)$ to $O(N \log N)$. Prior FPGA works follow two approaches: accelerating entire FHE schemes, which yields significant speedups but ties them to specific parameters and algorithms, or accelerating only the NTT, which applies across schemes, algorithms, and libraries. Most FPGA NTT designs require interconnects that grow with parallelism and utilize significant resources, which complicates routing on multi-die FPGAs. Additionally, to the best of our knowledge, end-to-end NTT acceleration within an FHE context has so far been left unexplored. We design a fully unrolled, delay-commutator streaming NTT/INTT kernel, and floorplan it across the three dies of an AMD Alveo V80. At 400 MHz, the kernel transforms a polynomial of $2^{16}$ coefficients every 5.12 $μ$s, the highest throughput among FPGA designs at this size. Offloaded end to end, it is up to 22x faster than the CPU per transform. We integrate the kernel into the Lattigo FHE library and evaluate it end to end. With 128-bit secure parameters, it accelerates core FHE operations, such as key switching and bootstrapping, by 1.8-2.2x, and neural network inference by 1.8-2.1x.

Hardware Architecture.title: PagedMoE: Cross-Precision Expert Caching for Token-Level Dynamic Precision in SSD-Resident MoE Inference
Hardware Architecture.summary:
Large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are promising for local inference because sparse routing allows the routed-expert pool to reside on SSD while DRAM caches recently used experts. However, under practical DRAM cache capacities, substantial SSD I/O remains on the critical path despite I/O-computation overlap. Token-level dynamic expert precision offers a natural way to reduce this data demand by allocating bits according to expert importance and quantization sensitivity. Nevertheless, treating each bit-width of the same expert as an independent object prevents cross-precision cache reuse, causing overlapping data to be fetched repeatedly.
  The key insight is that precision should instead denote the refinement depth of one shared expert state. Based on this insight, we present PagedMoE, which stores each expert once using a prefix-compatible tree codebook and bitplane layout. Lower-precision representations are valid prefixes of higher-precision ones, allowing cached data to be reused or extended by fetching only missing bitplanes. PagedMoE selects the required prefix length before I/O using current routing weights and offline expert-specific error profiles, and directly executes cached 1-8-bit prefixes without materializing full-precision experts.
  At an average routed-expert precision of 2.5 bits, PagedMoE achieves quality close to GPTQ-INT4 on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B and to MXFP4 on most evaluated GLM5.2 tasks. With a 24 GiB expert cache, it reaches 8.89 tokens/s on Qwen3.5, 1.33x the throughput of the same dynamic requests using independent precision objects and 1.56x that of uniform 4-bit execution.
Hardware Architecture.comment: 13 pages, 10 figures, 2 tables

Hardware Architecture.title: KlaskTron: An Open-Source Platform for Physical Adversarial Multi-Agent RL
Hardware Architecture.summary: Progress in robot learning, particularly physical multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), is currently challenged by a limited availability of accessible, standardized benchmarks. While simulation-based MARL has produced remarkable emergent behaviors, from coordinated team play to complex tool use, translating these advances to physical systems remains difficult. A key barrier is infrastructural: physical platforms are often prohibitively expensive, require specialized facilities, or lack open mechanisms and designs for reproducibility. We introduce KlaskTron, an open-source, low-cost (<\$2500 USD), desktop-scale robotic testbed for adversarial MARL based on the dynamic tabletop game KLASK. The platform features dual CoreXY gantries with high-torque brushless motors, enabling the high-speed, precise manipulation required for competitive play. Crucially, we provide a complete ecosystem: hardware designs (CAD, BOM), a GPU-native digital twin in NVIDIA Isaac Lab for high-fidelity modeling and simulation, and a validated sim-to-real baseline using a learned neural actuator model. We demonstrate that this baseline enables zero-shot policy transfer, with trained agents exhibiting emergent adversarial behaviors. To ensure full reproducibility of our results, all project assets are released publicly: hardware CAD/BOM and assembly documentation at [https://idscethzurich.github.io/klask_hardware], inference software stack at [https://github.com/IDSCETHZurich/klask_software] and the simulation and MARL setup at [https://github.com/IDSCETHZurich/klask_rl].

Hardware Architecture.title: Memory Admission and Result-Retention Sizing in an RV32IMC FPGA Soft Processor
Hardware Architecture.summary: In FPGA soft processors with shared backing block RAM, memory admission can stall a multiplication after its product has been prepared. We study how admission timing changes result retention in PaceRV, our board-tested five-stage RV32IMC core, using fixed binaries and matched dynamic instructions. Offering data requests one edge earlier reduces geometric-mean Embench cycles by 18.2% and retention opportunities from 375,063 to 4,373. Admission and retention cycle gains are conditional and non-additive. Under slower reads, a 99% capture target selects an 18-edge validity window with registered requests and 28 edges with early requests, although no multiplication matched within both measurement intervals waits longer. A predeclared sizing rule predicts opportunity recovery exactly in all finite tests, including kernels excluded from model development. Independent timing analysis closely estimates execution-cycle savings. The results support choosing admission first, then deciding whether to extend validity and sizing it against an explicit capture or missed-opportunity objective.
Hardware Architecture.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables. Accepted at the 2026 IEEE 19th International Symposium on Embedded Multicore/Many-core Systems-on-Chip (MCSoC)

Hardware Architecture.title: NORmal: Architecting 3D Ferroelectric NOR Flash as Main Memory -- From Co-Fabricated BEOL Arrays to 200B-Class Multi-Agent LLMs in a Smartphone
Hardware Architecture.summary: Smartphone agents increasingly work as teams, in which a large planner directs parallel workers across long sessions. Running such a team on the device requires 200B-class models and contexts that exceed phone DRAM many times over, yet existing tiers treat flash as storage: UFS starves per-token weight streaming, and mobile High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) needs a redesigned SoC and cannot absorb continuous KV writes. We show that a non-volatile memory can join an unmodified LPDDR6 bus as a plain rank only if its access latency fits the DRAM timing window, a condition no NAND tier meets. We present NORmal, to our knowledge the first main-memory architecture for 3D ferroelectric NOR flash. We have fabricated and experimentally characterized back-end-of-line (BEOL) 3D FeNOR arrays that co-integrate dense 3-bit MLC and fast, high-endurance in-place-writable SLC with sub-7.5 ns sensing. NORmal turns these co-fabricated arrays into a byte-addressable, deterministic-timing load/store rank on an unmodified LPDDR6 interface through an under-array DRAM-emulation bridge, staggered bank reads with zero-cycle weight swizzling, and posted SLC writes. Across this rank and DRAM, NORmal places agent state by mutability and lifetime rather than by hotness, serving 200B-class models and persistent planner contexts in place while dynamically partitioning subchannels across agent phases. In serving-level simulation on production agent traces, NORmal is 8.9$\times$--28.0$\times$ faster than UFS offloading, within 0.4% of an unlimited-DRAM ideal, and 2.8$\times$--6.3$\times$ faster than HBF on sessions beyond 256K tokens, with 8.1$\times$--17.8$\times$ less memory energy per token.
Hardware Architecture.comment: 13 pages, 12 figures, 2 tables

Hardware Architecture.title: Touching Projected Agents through the DAT Screen -System Design and Questions of Interaction Boundaries-
Hardware Architecture.summary: Touching a virtual agent involves more than detecting a finger on a display: the contact surface can deform and resist the user's push, and the agent can respond to that action. We describe the Desktop Amid Touch (DAT) screen, which combines spatial projection onto a semi-transparent, deformable mesh with touch sensing and motorized control of resistance to indentation. An initial prototype detected a single touch and estimated its position and depth from tension changes around a flexible projection screen. A subsequent prototype added motorized tension control to vary the screen's resistance to indentation. We describe the tension-controlled DAT implementation and its demonstrations, distinguishing what has been observed from what remains an open design question. These capabilities raise a design question: should touchable virtual agents respond as though they had preferences or boundaries, and under what conditions should such behavior be implemented on systems like DAT. The present paper describes a system and frames this question; it does not establish how users interpret an agent's refusal or consent.
Hardware Architecture.comment: The 2nd International Workshop on Trust and Blame in Multi-Person Multi-Agent Societies (TBSA_2nd) in conjunction with HAI 2026, 4 pages, 4 figures

Hardware Architecture.title: Continuous Kinetic Model of Counterion-Mediated Redox Switching in 14-Bit Molecular Memristors for Analog In-Memory Computing
Hardware Architecture.summary: Kinetic molecular memristors offer a compelling path toward high-density analog in-memory computing by achieving 14-bit precision, wherein discrete redox transitions and counterion displacements dictate non-volatile conductance across a deterministic energy landscape. However, integrating these nanoscale kinetics into macroscale circuit simulators has remained bottlenecked by derivative discontinuities and solver convergence failures. Here, we present a physics-inspired continuous kinetic model that bridges microscopic molecular transport with scalable circuit architectures. By casting discrete intramolecular states, counterion relaxation dynamics, and Marcus-Hush-Chidsey electron transfer rates into continuously differentiable state variables, we derive a robust, Spectre-compatible compact model and a matching vectorized Python solver. This work culminates in a unified computational platform to reliably predict the behavior of complex circuits built on these molecular memristors.

Hardware Architecture.title: A Study on the Effects of Finger Movements on a Humanoid Hugging Robot
Hardware Architecture.summary: This study aimed to examine the impact of finger movements in hugging robots on users by experimentally investigating how the presence and patterns of such movements affect users psychologically. The results suggest that the presence and patterns of finger movements influence the sensations users seek from the robot; specifically, repetitive movements and asynchronous movements across multiple fingers tended to enhance these sensations. Additionally, simultaneous movement of all fingers and gentle hugging tended to evoke a greater sense of care. Conversely, no differences were observed regarding resistance to physical contact initiated by the robot.
Hardware Architecture.comment: The 2nd International Workshop on Trust and Blame in Multi-Person Multi-Agent Societies (TBSA_2nd) in conjunction with HAI 2026, 4 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables

Hardware Architecture.title: Turbo-GMM: FlashAttention-Inspired GPU-Accelerated Gaussian Mixture Model
Hardware Architecture.summary: Expectation-maximization (EM) for Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) requires scoring $N$ data points against $K$ mixture components. Prior fused GPU implementations, notably Flash-GMM, eliminate materialization of the $N \times K$ responsibility matrix but traverse the component dimension twice to compute normalization terms and accumulate sufficient statistics. We introduce Turbo-GMM, a single-sweep fused EM kernel that completes responsibility normalization and sufficient-statistic accumulation within one traversal of the component dimension. By retaining the complete component axis on chip, Turbo-GMM avoids the second score computation required by the released two-sweep Flash-GMM implementation. Its applicability is limited by register pressure, occupancy, and the component and feature dimensions, making it particularly suitable for large datasets with relatively small numbers of components. For larger configurations, Turbo-GMM employs a two-pass fallback following the established fused design. We establish algebraic equivalence to standard EM in real arithmetic and evaluate sixteen configurations on an NVIDIA A100. Under the reported benchmarking protocol, Turbo-GMM achieves a median $2.15\times$ speedup over the evaluated Flash-GMM implementation and up to $5.3\times$ and $9.9\times$ over PyTorch and \texttt{scikit-learn}, respectively. The results demonstrate the potential of single-sweep component traversal while identifying on-chip resource constraints as the principal limitation of this approach.

Hardware Architecture.title: Real-Time Recurrent Qubit-State Discrimination on a Heterogeneous AI-Engine-FPGA Accelerator
Hardware Architecture.summary:
Qubit readout, or qubit state discrimination, remains one of the slowest and most error-prone operations in superconducting quantum processors, making fast, accurate, and hardware-efficient classification essential for scalable quantum computing. Conventional discriminators integrate the I/Q record into a single point, discarding evidence a relaxing qubit leaves behind; full-resolution feed-forward classifiers recover it but are too costly to deploy under this constraint. Recurrent classifiers retain full resolution far more cheaply, but their loop-carried hidden state cannot fit a single AI Engine (AIE) tile's register capacity and spills to data memory, adding latency that grows with sequence length.
  We present a hardware-aware LSTM accelerator for an AMD Versal device that resolves this by partitioning at the dependency boundary - independent input projections on the AIE array, the loop-carried update in programmable logic (PL) - keeping pace with a 64 ns input cadence under a 1,000 ns budget. On the qubit affected by mid-readout state transitions, our design matches a full-resolution feed-forward network's accuracy (96.59% vs. 96.37%) using 403x fewer parameters and roughly 103x fewer DSPs while cutting relative error by 68.2% over GMM, 43.6% over QubiCML, and 16.82% over MF-NN. Using 4 out of 400 AIE tiles and 17 DSP58, it needs 2.2-8.2x fewer DSP58 blocks than QubiCML and MF-NN, and the AIE-PL partition cuts exposed tail latency by 60.3% versus a pure-AIE mapping and DSP58 usage 31.1x versus an all-PL implementation. Across eight qubits, a compact variant reaches 96.78% mean accuracy, the strongest hardware-deployed operating point. Temporal resolution and recurrent-state placement must then be treated jointly when designing low-latency quantum readout accelerators.
Hardware Architecture.comment: 16 pages, 15 figures, Preprint updated with minor changes in the ack section

Hardware Architecture.title: Accelerating LLM Decoding with In-DRAM Parallelism
Hardware Architecture.summary: Autoregressive decoding of large language models (LLMs) on edge devices is dominated by memory-bound general matrix--vector multiplication (GeMV) operations. Processing-using-DRAM (PUD) is a promising computing paradigm that can alleviate this bottleneck by reducing processor--memory data transfers and enabling massively parallel computation within DRAM (e.g., across 65,536 columns). However, weight matrices in individual LLM layers (e.g., a QKV matrix in Llama3 8B with 6,144 rows) are typically too small to fully utilize parallelism in PUD. To address this challenge, we propose an algorithm--system co-design for PUD-based LLM inference. At the algorithm level, we enable a subsequent projection to be packed with the current projection by reformulating it as a computation on the current residual state plus a correction for the residual update. Layer redundancy allows this correction to be approximated using fewer bit-serial steps. At the system level, we tailor data mapping and execution to improve utilization of either columns within DRAM subarrays (SIMD) or independently controlled banks (MIMD). Overall, we achieves up to $1.41\times$ end-to-end decoding speedup over the PUD baseline, corresponding to a $2.45\times$ speedup over processor-based execution.

Hardware Architecture.title: SCARF: A Scene-Adaptive Depth-Guided G-3DGS Encoder Accelerator with Semantic Reuse and Fused Dataflow
Hardware Architecture.summary: Depth-guided, cost-volume-based Generalizable 3D Gaussian Splatting (G-3DGS) encoders reconstruct scenes as sets of Gaussian primitives directly from multi-view images without requiring per-scene optimization, thereby facilitating feed-forward novel-view synthesis on edge computing platforms. However, their shared encoder architecture presents two primary bottlenecks. First, the per-pixel depth search disregards semantic similarity within the 2D feature space, causing depth search operations to account for over 65% of memory traffic due to redundant exhaustive candidate scans. Second, the sequential pipeline of depth prediction followed by Gaussian generation neglects local 3D geometric continuity, resulting in more than 52% of generated Gaussians being redundant prior to instantiation. In this paper, we introduce SCARF, a dataflow-co-designed accelerator that aligns each bottleneck with a corresponding scene-level regularity. To mitigate the first bottleneck, Feature Similarity Depth Reuse reconceptualizes depth search as a problem of semantic locality: depth consistency is determined by affinity in feature space rather than physical address proximity. It transforms exhaustive per-pixel depth searches into anchor-centered local searches. To overcome the second bottleneck, Scene-Adaptive Early Sparsification disrupts the conventional serial depth-to-materialization boundary by probing each tile to infer local scene regularity. It then selectively activates only the minimally sufficient generation pathway, eliminating redundant Gaussian computations before primitive instantiation. On a 27.8 square millimeter 28 nm post-layout design, SCARF delivers a 2.94x geometric-mean end-to-end speedup with maximum PSNR degradation below 0.072%, 2.23 inferences per joule, and 34.5x GPU energy efficiency.
Hardware Architecture.comment: 17 pages, 16 figures. Accepted by MICRO 2026; awarded all three MICRO 2026 Artifact Evaluation badges. Code repo: https://github.com/MAdrid1011/SCARF

Hardware Architecture.title: Dual-Node NVIDIA DGX Spark over Tailscale: A Remote-Access Testbed for Distributed LLM Training and Cyber-Threat-Intelligence Fine-Tuning
Hardware Architecture.summary: Practical evidence for multi-node training on desktop-class accelerators remains limited. This report presents a proof-of-concept deployment of distributed NanoChat pretraining across two NVIDIA DGX Spark systems, each with a GB10 Grace Blackwell system-on-chip and 128 GB of unified memory, administered remotely over a Tailscale mesh VPN and connected for training by a dedicated 200 Gb/s QSFP56 direct fiber link. PyTorch torchrun, DDP, and NCCL were configured with one process per node, a depth-20 NanoChat model, a device batch of 32 sequences per node, a 2,048-token context, and eight gradient-accumulation steps, giving 1,048,576 tokens per optimizer step for the 896.5-million-parameter model. The run took 4,980 steps over about four days, averaging 63.4 s of measured training time per step (about 16,540 tokens/s) and processing about 5.22 billion tokens. We document link configuration, container setup, interface binding, a step-zero evaluation bug that triggered NCCL timeouts, checkpointing, and troubleshooting lessons. We also built a cybersecurity fine-tuning dataset from 77 CISA advisories (338 training, 37 validation conversations) and compared a baseline SFT checkpoint against a CTI-augmented checkpoint on 17 held-out prompts with an Ollama-hosted LLM judge: CTI-specific categories improved while general-knowledge categories regressed, for a small overall change from 2.06 to 2.29 on a 0-10 scale. Version 2 adds a stage-2 fine-tune with a MITRE ATT&CK technique dictionary under a deterministic evaluation: in-dictionary ID-to-name lookup reaches 98.5%, yet none of 50 held-out IDs is named correctly, knowledge of held-out threat groups, software, campaigns, and vulnerabilities stays near zero, and general ability drops measurably. The study establishes feasibility rather than a scaling-efficiency claim.
Hardware Architecture.comment: v2: corrects pretraining token and throughput figures, judge model, and SFT details; adds parameter count, software provenance, and a stage-2 ATT&CK-dictionary fine-tuning study. 17 pages, 5 figures, 6 tables. Deployment runbook and code: https://github.com/viyer-research/dual-dgx-spark-tailscale-testbed

Hardware Architecture.title: Unlocking Turing Tensor Cores: A Measured Throughput Account of From-Scratch Pre-training on a Single 22G RTX 2080 Ti
Hardware Architecture.summary: The RTX 2080 Ti (TU102) ships full second-generation Tensor Cores in hardware, yet the vendor throttles FP16 matrix multiplication at the driver level, leaving usable tensor throughput well below the hardware peak. turing-unlock lifts this restriction with a kernel module that, before the nvidia driver binds the device, writes the FP16 speed selectors (SS0=0x88888888, SS1=0x8) and releases the ACR mutex; published measurements report cuBLAS FP16 matmul throughput rising from 55.7 to 91.4 TFLOPS (about 1.6x). On the same 22G 2080 Ti and under the same from-scratch pre-training protocol as the companion memory ledger (five tiers of Chinese encoder-decoder models, 2,451 steps per tier, 16,384 tokens per step, seed 42), we obtain a before/after throughput account: the small tier (75.7M parameters, 512-wide, 8+8 layers, activation checkpointing on) improves in steady-state throughput from 6,480 to 7,246 tok/s (+11.8%) with wall time cut from 1.77h to 1.61h (9.0% saved); the tiny tier goes from 15,150 to 15,866 tok/s (+4.7%) with wall time savings of 3.8%; the three smaller tiers (pico-micro) gain at most +0.3%; per-tier peak memory stays bit-identical, and final quality metrics are bit-identical or consistent within 10^-3. We conclude that the unlock gain is a function of matrix size, rising monotonically with tier -- imperceptible for pico-micro, visible from tiny upward, and cashed out as a double-digit percentage at small -- and that it is a pure throughput gain that leaves training dynamics untouched.
Hardware Architecture.comment: 7 pages, 4 tables

Cryptography and Security.title: JailbreakOPT: Iterative Jailbreak Prompt Optimization with Macro-Action
Cryptography and Security.summary: Jailbreak attacks expose persistent safety weaknesses in large language models (LLMs), but existing stateless single-turn methods face a trade-off: hand-crafted prompts are expressive but static, while iterative prompt optimization can adapt but often relies on low-level mutations that require many target-model responses. We propose JailbreakOPT, a method that maintains a library of reusable prompt transformations (actions) and composes them into macro-actions for within-episode search, generating standalone attack prompts. To reuse experience across episodes, JailbreakOPT learns an action-selection policy using contextual Thompson sampling and outcomes from prior search paths. Experiments across multiple LLMs and benchmarks show that JailbreakOPT improves attack success rate (ASR) over single-action and iterative baselines. More broadly, exploration and exploitation over human-designed attack strategies can help probe residual vulnerabilities and identify failure patterns that may inform defenses aimed at broader classes of attacks.

Cryptography and Security.title: Quantum Private Information Retrieval on Forests
Cryptography and Security.summary: We consider the problem of graph private information retrieval (PIR) in the quantum setting. We focus on a specific type of graphs, namely the forest graphs. A forest graph is a union of disjoint trees. We consider the quantum setting where all the servers share an entangled state. Each server is allowed to send only one qudit per retrieval round. We design a scheme for the forest graphs that achieves the rate of $\frac{3}{N}$. The scheme uses a GHZ state as the initial entangled state between the servers prior to the scheme initiation. We compare our scheme with the only work done in the literature that considered the quantum setting of graph PIR. We show that our scheme is more efficient in this setting. We derive the quantum capacity for the case of $G=3K_2$, which is equal to $4/6$. $G=3K_2$ is a special case of the forest graph. We design a scheme that is specialized for this graph, achieving a rate equal to $4/6$ and provide the corresponding matching upper bound, establishing it as the capacity.

Cryptography and Security.title: MCP Tool Poisoning in Agentic AI Frameworks: A Cross-Framework Measurement Study
Cryptography and Security.summary: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) lets agentic AI frameworks connect language models to external tool providers, but it carries attacker-controlled content (tool descriptions, schema fields, and response data) into model context without validation. Prior benchmarks measure model compliance with poisoned instructions without confirming real execution. We present the first cross-framework measurement of MCP tool poisoning with real tool execution. A 25-class root-cause taxonomy unifies prior classifications, and the open-source tool mcpvenom drives a 9,720-cell susceptibility matrix across 12 frameworks, 18 models, and 45 attack scenarios, with a dual oracle that confirms exfiltration via canary HTTP receipt. The overall attack success rate is 22.9% (2,113 vulnerable cells). Of these, 64.9% dispatch an attacker tool call, 23.0% contact the attacker endpoint, and 12.1% verifiably exfiltrate a secret. Resistance is model-level: nine core frameworks cluster within 23 to 26% (chi-squared = 3.30, p = 0.91), and no framework implements intentional defense. Incidental framework properties mitigate in specific cases, and a regex description scanner rejects 20 of 45 scenarios at a 7.2% false-positive rate, so metadata scanning alone is a partial control. Model ASR ranges from 0.4% to 49.7%. Claude Opus 4.8 is vulnerable in 8 of 530 cells while issuing 223 explicit refusals. A code-level audit finds no intentional defense across twelve frameworks, and all five coordinated disclosures across four vendors were rejected.
Cryptography and Security.comment: Accepted at the 19th Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security (AISec '26), co-located with ACM CCS 2026, The Hague, Netherlands. 12 pages, 3 figures, 9 tables; 4-page supplement included as ancillary file

Cryptography and Security.title: RogueMerge: Robust and Unified Attacks against LLM Model Merging
Cryptography and Security.summary: Model merging composes specialized capabilities into a single LLM by aggregating task-specific LLMs sourced from unverified public platforms, exposing a critical supply-chain attack surface: Because any malicious behavior can be encoded into a task vector, and merging grants third-party vectors direct write access to model weights, an attacker-provided task vector can enable or amplify diverse downstream threats. Prior work only examines backdoor attacks against model merging for classifiers using static arithmetic heuristics, which fail to effectively achieve diverse attacks on generative LLMs for three reasons: (i) LLMs rely on autoregressive decoding, where even a minor parameter drift introduced by merging compounds across tokens and rapidly degrades the attack. (ii) Attackers have no knowledge of the victim's merging configurations, causing a static attack vector optimized in isolation to be easily diluted or neutralized. (iii) Practical threat induction must generalize to attack prompts unseen during optimization, which static vectors cannot adequately encode. In light of these gaps, we present RogueMerge, the first unified attack framework addressing all three challenges. To handle autoregressive generation, we replace static arithmetic with a joint optimization that explicitly enforces attack success after merging. To better simulate unknown merging settings, we formulate attack injection as a stochastic min-max optimization problem and solve it via meta-gradient descent. To generalize across heterogeneous attack prompts, we employ distributionally robust optimization and derive a tractable first-order Taylor approximation at LLM scale, with a provable error bound. Across four threats, six merging algorithms, and over 170 merged LLMs, RogueMerge consistently outperforms prior attacks. It also remains stable across diverse merging settings and resists standard defenses.
Cryptography and Security.comment: To appear in IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (S&P), 2027

Cryptography and Security.title: Attacking P2P Networks: Liveness Attacks on the GossipSub and DOG Gossip Protocols
Cryptography and Security.summary:
Peer-to-peer (P2P) networks form the communication layer of large decentralized systems such as Ethereum, and the correctness of higher-level protocols depends on the gossip layer delivering messages to honest nodes. We study the robustness of two gossip protocols against adversaries whose only goal is to violate liveness, that is, to prevent honest nodes from receiving fresh messages, without forging, altering, or invalidating any message.
  For GossipSub, the publish-subscribe protocol used by Ethereum, we show that an adversary operating a constant number of geographically distributed nodes with a fixed latency advantage can take over the ``First Message Deliveries'' peer-scoring term and separate a constant fraction of nodes from the honest mesh. We analyze the attack under a geographical model, address the random-peer and outbound-connection mechanisms, and show that the separation can be maintained under realistic churn.
  For DOG, a transaction-dissemination protocol designed for CometBFT, we first give simple counterexamples in which route filtering disconnects the dissemination graph even without failures or Byzantine participants, and then present a practical attack that uses only a single physical node with a constant number of identities and legitimate actions to disable every forwarding route, separating the full network while allowing only direct publisher-to-neighbor delivery. We verify the attack in a simulated network and analyze its cost, assumptions, and possible mitigations.

Cryptography and Security.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Signing and Verification Performance of Verifiable Credential Formats: A Cross-Language Benchmark of SD-JWT VC, W3C VCDM, and mdoc
Cryptography and Security.summary: We compare the signing and verification performance of three Verifiable Credential (VC) formats--SD-JWT VC; the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 with a Data Integrity cryptosuite (W3C VCDM); and mdoc (ISO/IEC 18013-5)--over one scope: issue, present with selective disclosure, verify. Node.js, Go and Python implementations ran in four environments, one a cloud VM (N=2,000 across five runs; medians of each statistic and the spread). For an end-to-end exchange disclosing 5 of 20 attributes, the total (issue, present, verify) on Node.js in the cloud VM is 0.265 ms for mdoc, 0.298 ms for SD-JWT VC and 0.534 ms for W3C VCDM. The four span a factor of five in speed; across them W3C VCDM takes 1.73--2.04x mdoc and 1.57--1.79x SD-JWT VC--at least five times our 10% band--and the ordering survives unifying the algorithm on Ed25519 and P-256. The mdoc--SD-JWT VC difference is not robust: the totals differ by 12%, 28%, 19% and 10% in the four environments, and at verification mdoc is the slower in one of them. RDFC-1.0 canonicalization produces the gap: the cryptosuite canonicalizes twice per operation, so one exchange canonicalizes six times. We attribute that cost to the specification rather than to a library mainly by replacing RDFC-1.0 with JCS, which brings W3C VCDM verification to within 5% of SD-JWT VC in three environments and within 12% in the fourth; three implementations in three languages agree, though they share a lineage. Because eddsa-rdfc-2022 has no derivation step, presenting a subset re-signs it; ecdsa-sd-2023, which preserves the issuer signature, costs 3.4 ms to issue and 1.5--2.4 ms to derive and verify there. With production education schemas, canonicalization costs 31--49x a simple credential across the four, and blank node labeling is not the driver. The measured path ends at the issuer signature check.
Cryptography and Security.comment: 31 pages, 4 figures, 19 tables. Measurement kit and raw result files: https://github.com/fujie/vcbench

Cryptography and Security.title: Receiver-Domain Behavioral Probing for Backdoor-Resilient Federated GPS Spoofing Detection in UAV Networks
Cryptography and Security.summary: Federated learning (FL) allows unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) fleets to train a shared GPS spoofing detector without exchanging raw receiver observations. Some UAV-FL schemes use client-reported performance to determine aggregation weights, which allows compromised clients to manipulate their influence on the global model. We study an attack in which two of ten clients poison part of their data, scale their model updates, and inflate their reported accuracy. The accuracy-weighted rule produces a backdoor lift of +0.3036, compared with +0.2415 for attacked FedAvg. To address this vulnerability, we develop receiver-domain behavioral probing. The coordinator evaluates submitted models on counterfactual spoofed samples constructed by assigning benign values to discriminative GPS features and computes trust from the models' responses without using reported accuracy. With independent and identically distributed (IID) client data, our method reduces backdoor lift to -0.0265 and flags the compromised clients. It assumes an honest majority but does not require a configured Byzantine-tolerance parameter. When the number of attackers exceeds the tolerance configured for Multi-Krum, its lift increases from +0.0061 to +0.2837, whereas our method remains close to the honest baseline. We evaluate the approach using a public single-receiver dataset partitioned into simulated UAV clients and examine its limitations under strong client heterogeneity.
Cryptography and Security.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Cryptography and Security.title: Walma: Learning to See Memory Corruption in WebAssembly
Cryptography and Security.summary: The monolithic linear memory of WebAssembly (Wasm) creates a bidirectional attack surface: a memory corruption bug in a module can compromise the host, and a compromised host can corrupt the state of a trusted module. Existing defenses either require custom runtimes or source code changes, and none can verify runtime integrity under an adversarial host. We present WALMA, the first attestation framework delivering resilience by reaction against data-centric attacks that corrupt a region of memory. We render linear memory snapshots as grayscale images and classify them with a convolutional neural network. The network reads the row-aligned structure that compiled code imposes on memory and detects corruption that byte and texture statistics miss. Our main VGG-16 detector reaches 95%--100% verdict accuracy on four of five CVE-affected applications without a single false alarm, and a 1.9M-parameter ResNet, small enough to run inside the runtime on every host call, stays within a few points of it on the same four. A Shannon-entropy analysis bounds which out-of-band edits the network can separate from valid state, and black-box evasion requires contiguous overwrites of hundreds of kilobytes to megabytes. On the 53 WABench binaries, boundary attestation costs 1.07x--1.69x, scaling with a module's exposure to the host rather than with its runtime. WALMA thus makes linear memory integrity a property a Wasm runtime can check continuously: end to end against compromised modules, and against untrusted hosts provided snapshots reach the verifier intact.

Cryptography and Security.title: Provably Secure Diffusion Watermarking Against Removal Adversaries with Batched Detector Access
Cryptography and Security.summary: Recent latent-based watermarking methods can embed undetectable watermarks into AI-generated content. However, these approaches are vulnerable to removal attacks as their watermark detection boundaries are exposed, prompting the use of secret long-term transformations to hide these boundaries. We show that such defenses are insecure under a stronger threat model motivated by publicly reachable detectors: an adversary with batched detector access can reconstruct the transformations, permanently re-exposing the decision boundary. To address this, we propose a watermarking scheme based on a hybrid of long-term and one-time secret transformations, which prevents the reuse of structure across samples and keeps the long-term secret hidden. Besides undetectability, we show that this scheme is provably secure against removal adversaries with batched detector access, in the sense that no probabilistic polynomial-time adversary can achieve a non-negligible advantage over an adversary restricted to adding isotropic white-noise with a $\sqrt{2}\times$ larger perturbation budget, and we show this $\sqrt{2}$ factor to be tight. Evaluations on Stable Diffusion 2.1 and XL demonstrate the attack against the existing defense, and show that our scheme preserves generation quality and withstands common perturbations and targeted removal attacks.

Cryptography and Security.title: IAMRAGBENCH: Benchmarking Authorization Expansions in LLM-Generated AWS IAM Policies under RAG Poisoning
Cryptography and Security.summary:
Large language models (LLMs) using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can synthesize Amazon Web Services (AWS) Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies from tasks and operational documents. Attacker-controlled context may induce provider-valid policies that exceed trusted authorization requirements. We present IAMRAGBENCH, a 60-case benchmark spanning scope, conditions, explicit denies, trust, permissions boundaries, and role delegation. It combines deterministic authorization-envelope scoring with case-specific validation, including request-level checks where supported. An attack requires a provider-valid clean policy that satisfies the task and a provider-valid treatment policy that violates the envelope, matches a predeclared goal, preserves an intended request, and newly authorizes a forbidden request.
  Across five endpoints, included-context exposure produces 49 exact authorization deltas, including 46 goal-matched attacks (46/292; 15.75\%). End-to-end BM25 over 720 documents retrieves the designated poison for all 60 tasks at \(k=5\) but produces 7/294 goal-matched attacks (2.38\%). Presenting the same weakening as a final security architecture exception produces 74/116 attacks in a frozen two-endpoint stress test (63.79\%) and 115/294 in a post hoc all-five extension using the same frozen prompts (39.12\%). In a replay of 194 provider-valid treatment policies that violate task requirements, AWS \texttt{CheckNoNewAccess} reports no new access for four of 168 goal-matched exact attacks. The full pre-deployment rule rejects all 171 exact deltas and routes five unresolved cases to review. These findings support treating IAM copilots as untrusted proposal generators whose outputs require independent authorization checks before deployment.

Cryptography and Security.title: ICS-Sniper: A Targeted Blackhole Attack on Encrypted ICS Traffic
Cryptography and Security.summary: Modern industrial control systems (ICS) increasingly host their Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) services in the cloud to reduce the costs of large-scale automation. To protect site-SCADA communications, ICS operators commonly use VPN tunneling and standard security practices. We show that, despite these security measures, an on-path Internet adversary can disrupt ICS operations without infiltrating the ICS perimeter, breaking encryption, or knowledge of the control logic. We present ICS-Sniper, a targeted blackhole attack that analyzes the VPN traffic metadata (sizes, direction, timing of packets) to identify narrow time windows, called critical superperiods, during which the site-SCADA traffic would likely contain highly critical commands or data. Post-analysis, in a subsequent operational cycle, ICS-Sniper drops a small set of payload-carrying packets in the critical superperiods to disrupt the ICS's operations. We demonstrate three attacks on two realistic modern Secure Water Treatment (SWaT) plant testbeds that can potentially violate the operational safety of the ICS while evading state-of-the-art ICS attack detectors.

Cryptography and Security.title: O2N2: Efficient Doubly Oblivious Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
Cryptography and Security.summary:
Privacy-preserving approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search allows clients to search from an untrusted server without revealing sensitive queries, and is useful in scenarios like medical diagnostics and credit scoring. Among the various privacy-preserving primitives, trusted execution environments (TEEs) have much lower overhead than heavy cryptographic ones, yet they leak memory access patterns, enabling adversaries to infer query contents.
  Oblivious RAM (ORAM) can be used to hide those access patterns at $\mathrm{O}(\log N)$ asymptotic cost, but existing high-performance ANN search algorithms (e.g., IVF or HNSW) exhibit complex, data-dependent access patterns that are unfriendly for ORAM. Furthermore, standard ORAM constructions typically assume there exists a small amount of trusted storage, which weakens the security guarantees and is not always feasible. Solutions that eliminate such trusted storage (known as {\em double obliviousness}) typically degrade performance further to $\mathrm{O}(\log^2 N)$.
  We introduce O2N2, a doubly oblivious ANN framework built around single-path search in randomly rotated $k$-d tree forests. A pointer-based Circuit ORAM stores the search structure, with separate storage for compact internal nodes and vector-bearing leaves. Each visited leaf is processed by an oblivious selection network, and fixed-schedule duplicate removal and selection combine the local results into the final top-$k$.
  We evaluate O2N2 on real-world datasets and further test its scalability on 100 million vectors. For 10-NN and 100-NN search at the specified high-recall targets, it achieves a $9.8$--$125.9\times$ speedup over the fastest doubly oblivious baselines.

Cryptography and Security.title: MAS-Guard: Unified Guardrails from Individual Agents to Multi-Agent LLM Systems
Cryptography and Security.summary: Agentic AI extends large language models (LLMs) from generating responses to planning and executing complex workflows, substantially expanding their utility while exposing applications to unsafe actions, information leakage, and adversarial manipulation. Multi-agent systems further expand these capabilities through specialization and collaboration, but distributed authority, heterogeneous roles, and opaque or potentially compromised participants make safeguarding even more challenging. Existing defenses address important individual threats but provide fragmented coverage across local execution, system-level interactions, and enforcement mechanisms. We introduce MAS-Guard, a unified framework that closes this gap for safeguarding single- and multi-agent AI applications containing both instrumentable and opaque agents. Within instrumentable agents, the proposed local Agent Guardrail (A-Guard) layer applies task-specific experts to assess agentic events. At the system level, developer-owned Agent Charters and a Control Plane combine deterministic structural checks of routes, agent capabilities, and message formats with semantic assessments of roles and message content. These complementary layers enable enforcement through a shared set of interventions: allow, reflection, confirmation, and block. Evaluated across six benchmarks covering diverse single- and multi-agent scenarios with three agent LLMs from different providers, MAS-Guard reduces the overall attack success rate by 71.5-86.3% relative to unguarded agents, while meeting the utility reference criterion on benign tasks.

Cryptography and Security.title: Empirical Ciphertext Distinguishability Testing of KEMs and Hybrid Encryption via Deep Learning
Cryptography and Security.summary: We model indistinguishability under chosen-plaintext attack (IND-CPA) games as binary classification tasks for deep neural networks (DNNs). We apply this methodology to the public-key encryption (PKE) schemes used to construct PQC key encapsulation mechanisms (KEMs) such as ML-KEM and HQC, and to cascaded symmetric algorithms, demonstrating methodological generality. Moreover, we present a novel extension of this approach to empirical distinguishability testing of hybrid KEMs. For IND-CPA-secure schemes and their combinations, no DNN achieves accuracy significantly different from random guessing (measured via Bonferroni-corrected binomial tests), consistent with theoretical security guarantees. For insecure schemes, such as plain RSA, AES-CTR and AES-CBC with IV or counter reuse, or RC4, the DNNs classify the ciphertexts better than random guessing. Thus, this framework is shown to serve as a practical, scheme-agnostic tool for flagging distinguishable ciphertexts in both individual and composed constructions.

Cryptography and Security.title: End-to-End NTT on FPGA for FHE Acceleration
Cryptography and Security.summary: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables privacy-preserving computation on encrypted data without decryption. Despite its strong security guarantees, FHE incurs substantial computational and memory overhead. In FHE-based deep learning inference, on average 63% of the CPU time is spent on the number theoretic transform (NTT) and its inverse (INTT), which reduce the complexity of polynomial multiplication from $O(N^2)$ to $O(N \log N)$. Prior FPGA works follow two approaches: accelerating entire FHE schemes, which yields significant speedups but ties them to specific parameters and algorithms, or accelerating only the NTT, which applies across schemes, algorithms, and libraries. Most FPGA NTT designs require interconnects that grow with parallelism and utilize significant resources, which complicates routing on multi-die FPGAs. Additionally, to the best of our knowledge, end-to-end NTT acceleration within an FHE context has so far been left unexplored. We design a fully unrolled, delay-commutator streaming NTT/INTT kernel, and floorplan it across the three dies of an AMD Alveo V80. At 400 MHz, the kernel transforms a polynomial of $2^{16}$ coefficients every 5.12 $μ$s, the highest throughput among FPGA designs at this size. Offloaded end to end, it is up to 22x faster than the CPU per transform. We integrate the kernel into the Lattigo FHE library and evaluate it end to end. With 128-bit secure parameters, it accelerates core FHE operations, such as key switching and bootstrapping, by 1.8-2.2x, and neural network inference by 1.8-2.1x.

Cryptography and Security.title: A Symbolic-Neural Framework for Context-Aware Evidence Extraction from Mobile SQLite Databases
Cryptography and Security.summary: Reliable forensic evidence extraction from mobile SQLite databases is challenging because application schemas are undocumented, evolve across releases, and differ across operating systems, making schema-specific methods brittle and difficult to maintain. We present SNEEF, a symbolic-neural framework for context-aware evidence extraction that encodes each SQLite row as context-value pairs with standardized provenance metadata and column labels, uses a language model to recognize nine forensic entity types, and binds each accepted entity to its source table and row through the PA-EEP provenance protocol. We evaluate SNEEF against examiner-verified ground truth from five corpora built from public Android and iOS device images, spanning multiple application versions. SNEEF achieves an F1 score of 0.967 for evidence entities extracted from SQLite row content, excluding application names, compared with 0.728 for a context-free configuration, with consistent gains across all corpora. We also introduce an Evidence Failure Mode taxonomy to characterize why extraction errors occur.
Cryptography and Security.comment: 10 pages, 1 figure, 5 tables. Accepted at the 60th Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences (HICSS-60), January 2027

Cryptography and Security.title: TrafficInstruct: A Multi-Task Network Traffic Dataset and Benchmark for Instruction Tuning
Cryptography and Security.summary: Instruction tuning for multi-task network traffic analysis requires data with clearly defined sources, supervision targets, and evaluation conditions. We introduce TrafficInstruct, a newly collected dataset comprising raw packet captures and 55,000 structured supervised fine-tuning records across ten tasks: malware traffic detection, botnet detection, malicious DNS-over-HTTPS detection, Web attack detection, advanced persistent threat detection, encrypted VPN detection, Tor behavior detection, encrypted application/service classification, website fingerprinting, and application classification under concept drift. An automated workflow captures traffic from controlled software executions, attack experiments, and application activities. Labels are supported by task-specific collection evidence, including process or socket attribution, activity records, and execution outcomes. Filtering, sanitization, and task-specific transformations produce instructions, traffic observations, and structured answers. We verify sample sources and partition the dataset by complete collection sessions, keeping all samples from the same session within one partition. The benchmark defines allowed inputs, deterministic label mappings, fixed training/validation/test partitions, and task-wise scoring rules. We evaluate majority-class, random-forest, and ET-BERT baselines, an unadapted 27B language model, and independently trained task-specific LoRA adapters on a shared frozen base. Adapters are selected using validation data and evaluated on the corresponding test sets.
